content: Goal: orient before proposing. Action: listed workspace root. Observation: read-only session, no shell; task states frozen budget 3000 Stage2 epochs / 24 steps / 24556 items, Stage3 recall@10 target 0.065. Prior rounds already covered: successor-weighted Frechet codebook updates (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook), curvature set by measured hard prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), behaviour-ranked radial radius from context entropy (BRad-RQ), Lorentz successor-profile smoothing, behaviour cones, successor-boost geodesic shift, branch-curvature MoE. Open: pick an untouched coupling position.

Goal: choose a coupling position untouched by the six/seven earlier rounds. Action: reviewed workspace root (progress.jsonl only, no repo files readable) and the round history in the task text. Observation: earlier rounds all preserved the baseline fixed code budget per prefix and instead (a) weighted codebook updates by successors, (b) set per-level curvature from transition hardness, (c) set per-item radial radius from context entropy, (d) smoothed successor profiles in Lorentz space, (e) built behaviour cones, (f) applied successor-boosted geodesic shifts, (g) added branch-curvature MoE. The untouched corner is the SID *prefix capacity structure* itself: how many codewords each prefix subtree is allowed. Reasoning: changing N_p changes which argmin (and therefore which token) is produced, so it is a real quantizer change, not a loss term; and both the behaviour term (transition mass m_p) and the curved term (hyperbolic Fréchet spread sigma_p) are jointly necessary to compute N_p, so the coupling is one pathway. Also verified that pure geodesic transport of the residual chain is an isometry and hence vacuous (same argmin) - recorded as a rejected sub-design so it is not smuggled in. Open: write the minimal spec, safeguards and cost.

IDEA: BRANCHCAP-HYPFANOUT
TITLE: Behaviour-branching hyperbolic capacity allocation: the number of SID slots each prefix subtree owns is derived from training transition mass and hyperbolic successor spread.
MOTIVATION: An RQ-VAE SID gives every first-level prefix exactly the same number of child codewords. User behaviour is not uniform: a few prefixes are transition hubs whose continuations fan out broadly, while many prefixes lead to a narrow, almost deterministic next item. Uniform fanout spends most of the second/third-level capacity on prefixes with almost no future traffic and starves the hubs, so quantization error is concentrated exactly where the generative recommender samples next tokens most often.
NOVELTY: Earlier rounds kept the fanout schedule fixed and changed codebook update weights (Poincare-Frechet successors), per-level curvature (CURVCTRL-SID), per-item radius (BRad-RQ), Lorentz profile smoothing, cones, geodesic shifts or MoE branching. Here the *structure* of the code changes: the per-prefix code budget N_p is a derived quantity, and each prefix owns a disjoint contiguous slice of the level codebook, so prefixes get unequal numbers of SID children. Nothing in the repo allocates codebook capacity, and nothing derives a capacity from a hyperbolic spread of successors.
CHANGE: At every level l>=2 the total slot budget N is split across prefixes by the high-rate quantization rule N_p proportional to (m_p * sigma_p^2)^(D/(D+2)), where m_p is the training transition mass leaving the prefix and sigma_p is the hyperbolic (Lorentz) Fréchet spread of that prefix's training successors; the level-l assignment argmin is then restricted to prefix p's own slice of N_p codewords.
SPECIFICATION: Build W (top-M row-normalised directed transition counts) and m_p from training sequences only; measure s = median latent norm at init and fix K = -1/s^2; at every C epochs map the EMA latent table to the Lorentz model, compute for each prefix p the weighted Riemannian Fréchet mean and spread (5 fixed gradient steps), allocate N_p by largest-remainder rounding of (m_p sigma_p^2)^(D/(D+2)) with integer floor 1, rebuild each prefix's codebook slice by 5-step warm-started k-means, and keep the standard EMA codeword update between refreshes.
COST: Negligible. Encoder/decoder/Stage3 cost unchanged; the level-level argmin is the same size (every item still scans its own prefix slice, total N codewords). Added work is one allocation refresh per C=100 epochs: 30 refreshes over 3000 epochs, each 24556*8 = 196,448 successor pairs, 5 Frechet iterations and 5 k-means iterations in ambient dim D+1 (D=32) = about 1.6e7 flops per refresh, about 5e8 flops and a few MB of table gathers in total. Per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch) the added cost is one slice-offset lookup, i.e. below 0.5% wall clock; the transition matrix is built once before training.
HYPOTHESIS: If capacity follows behaviour branching in curved latent space, then high-mass/high-spread prefixes will receive visibly more level-2 slots (spread of N_p across prefixes clearly above 1), the fraction of training transitions whose successor shares the item's level-2 prefix will rise, and Stage 3 test recall@10 will exceed 0.065 with one run.
RISKS: sigma_p may be nearly constant across prefixes, so the both-on allocation collapses to the uniform schedule and the run is a baseline run; capacity concentration can starve low-mass prefixes and raise collisions for long-tail tar

gets; the C=100 warm-start reallocation could oscillate and destabilise the EMA codebooks; D/(D+2) exponent near 1 makes the allocation close to proportional-to-mass, so the geometry term may be too weak to matter; the generative recommender's per-level vocabulary becomes level-dependent in size, which needs a careful token-space remap.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: User-interest branching as directed item transitions aggregated per prefix: the transition mass m_p and the successor multiset of each prefix.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: One restricted pass over Stage 2 training sequences only. For each consecutive pair (i_t, i_t+1), c[i_t, i_t+1] += 1. Row-normalise, keep top M=8 successors per item (documented default), renormalise the kept rows, and store m_i = sum_j c_ij (log1p for stability). For a prefix p, m_p = sum over i in S_p of m_i and the successor multiset is the union of the kept rows of all i in S_p with summed weights.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: W, m_p, the successor multisets and the median norm scale s are computed exclusively from the training-split sequences (and, for sigma_p, from encoder latents of training items). Validation and test sequences are never read during SID construction, allocation or codebook refreshes; the item catalogue is the frozen training catalogue, so no validation or test interaction can enter a SID token.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Lorentz model of constant negative curvature K = -1/s^2 with radius s = median training latent norm measured once at initialisation (measured scale, not tuned). Operations: exp_0^K, distance d_K(a,b) = s * arccosh(-<a,b>_L / s^2) with signature (-,+), and weighted Riemannian (Karcher) Frechet mean by fixed-step gradient descent.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In quantization capacity allocation: at every C-th epoch boundary, inside the RQ-VAE codebook-budget schedule, before the level-l slice-restricted nearest-codeword assignment and the corresponding k-means slice rebuild.
COUPLING PATH: training transition graph -> per-prefix behaviour mass m_p and successor multiset -> per-prefix curved spread sigma_p around the Lorentz Frechet mean -> derived slot count N_p -> the prefix's codebook slice -> slice-restricted argmin -> level-l SID token -> Stage 3 prompt tokens. Removing behaviour makes m_p and the successor multiset uninformative (uniform allocation); removing curvature changes the mean and the spread (Euclidean variance gives a different N_p); either change moves the argmin and hence the emitted token.
COUPLING EQUATION: N_p = max(1, LR_round( N * (m_p * sigma_p^2)^(D/(D+2)) / sum_p' (m_p' * sigma_p'^2)^(D/(D+2)) )), with sigma_p^2 = sum_j w_j d_K(m_p^*, x_j)^2 / sum_j w_j and m_p^* = argmin_x sum_j w_j d_K(x, x_j)^2, where w_j are the behaviour transition weights and d_K is the Lorentz distance of curvature K = -1/s^2.
OBSERVABLES: Distribution (min/median/max, entropy) of N_p at level 2 and 3; per-level code usage entropy; successor prefix predictability, i.e. the fraction of training transitions whose successor shares the source item's level-1 and level-2 prefix; SID collision count and prefix counts; the allocation computed for the behaviour-off and geometry-off configurations as static diagnostics (no extra training); and Stage 3 test_recall@10.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: m_p and the successor multiset replaced by the prefix's own item count and the prefix's own items, i.e. w_j = 1 for j in S_p, so the allocation sees no transitions. This arm exists in code behind BEHAVIOUR_ON=False, is unit-checked, is c

omputed once as a static diagnostic, and is never trained.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: BEHAVIOUR_ON=True but K set to 0 in the allocation branch, so the Frechet mean becomes the weighted Euclidean mean and sigma_p becomes the weighted Euclidean standard deviation, giving a different N_p. Exists behind GEOMETRY_ON=False, unit-checked, static diagnostic only, never trained.
ABLATION BOTH ON: The single trained configuration: transition weights AND Lorentz curvature-(-1/s^2) Frechet spread both active, producing N_p and the slice-restricted level assignments. One training run, 3000 Stage 2 epochs, frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping, no seed repetition.
SPEC EQUATIONS: (1) c_ij = count of consecutive (i,j) in training sequences; W_ij = c_ij / sum_j' c_ij', top-M=8 kept and renormalised; m_i = sum_j c_ij. (2) s = median_i ||mu_i||_2 at init; K = -1/s^2; x_i = exp_0^K(mu_i). (3) d_K(a,b) = s*arccosh(-<a,b>_L/s^2). (4) For prefix p: weights w_j aggregated over S_p; m_p = sum_j w_j; x_p^(0) = exp_0^K( sum_j w_j mu_j / m_p ); for t = 0..4: g = -2 sum_j w_j log_{x_p^(t)}(x_j) / m_p; x_p^(t+1) = exp_{x_p^(t)}( eta_t g ), eta_t = s/(2 sqrt(t+1)); m_p^* = x_p^(5). (5) sigma_p^2 = sum_j w_j d_K(m_p^*, x_j)^2 / m_p, with sigma_p clipped to the [q05, q95] quantiles of {sigma_p} measured on the same epoch's prefixes. (6) alpha = D/(D+2); a_p = (m_p sigma_p^2)^alpha; N_p = max(1, floor(N a_p / sum a_p)) then distribute the deficit by largest remainder so sum N_p = N. (7) Slice offsets o_p = cumulative sum of N_p; level-l assignment for item i with prefix p: k_l(i) = argmin_{k in [o_p, o_p + N_p)} || r_l(i) - C_l[k] ||_2^2; codewords of the slice initialised by 5-step warm-started k-means on the residuals of S_p and then EMA-updated as in the baseline. (8) Refreshes every C = 100 epochs (30 refreshes total), between-epochs only.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: training-only transition counts, the EMA latent table over 24556 items, the current prefix assignment from the previous epoch, the level slot budget N, the residual dimension D, and the measured scale s. Outputs: integer per-prefix slot counts N_p, contiguous slice offsets o_p, per-prefix initialised codebook rows, and the slice-restricted codeword indices that become the SID tokens.
SAFEGUARDS: sigma_p clipped to measured q05/q95 quantiles of the same epoch to avoid one degenerate prefix owning the whole budget; N_p floored at 1 and capped at N - (P - 1) so every prefix keeps at least one child; largest-remainder rounding guarantees sum N_p = N exactly; log and arccosh inputs are clamped (cosh argument to 1 + 1e-7, arccosh input >= 1 + 1e-7) and norm denominators floored at 1e-8; the Frechet gradient step is capped at radius s so no exp map leaves the chart; allocation refreshes are limited to epoch boundaries with warm-started k-means so the EMA codebooks do not oscillate; the transition graph is frozen once before training so no test/validation interaction can leak in; the level token vocabulary is remapped deterministically from the global slot index so the generative recommender sees a stable token space.
END IDEA
